options.why: array type i can have a two-byte minimum size; the guard chooses a wider signed type when needed for indices and counts.
These arrays hold numeric links and counters, not strings, so string storage does not explain the width guard.
Counts are bounded by the input size; they still need more than a two-byte signed range can guarantee.
Character labels use the separate unsigned-byte array; the width decision protects signed links and counts.

items.explanation: The specification permits a 2-byte minimum for i.
